When to book

Four to six weeks is comfortable. Two is a scramble.

Nobody wants to explain to a five-year-old that the castle wasn't available. Here's when the calendar tightens up:

Spring and summer weekends — October to March is peak. Saturday mornings go first.
Long weekends and school holidays — Suppliers block these out early — often two months ahead.
The fortnight before Christmas — The busiest run of the year for entertainers and castles.

Questions parents ask

Kids party entertainment FAQs

How much does kids party entertainment cost in Australia?
Most kids party entertainers charge for a one to two hour package. As a guide, face painters and balloon twisters usually sit at the lower end, all-rounder entertainers and magicians in the middle, and multi-performer character packages at the top. Play hire is priced by the set and the hire window rather than by the hour. Send one brief through Kids Party House and you'll get itemised quotes to compare rather than a single ballpark figure.
How far in advance should I book a kids party entertainer?
Four to six weeks is comfortable for most weekends. Book earlier — eight weeks or more — if your party falls in the spring and summer peak, on a long weekend, or in the fortnight before Christmas, because that's when Saturday mornings go first. If your date is close, send your brief anyway; availability moves around and cancellations happen.
What's the difference between soft play hire and a jumping castle?
Soft play is a padded, ground-level play area — blocks, mini slides, rockers, ball pits and fencing — designed for babies through to about five. A jumping castle is an inflatable that needs power, anchoring and open ground, and suits roughly three years and up. Parties with a wide age range often book both: soft play for the little ones and a castle for the older siblings.
What entertainment works best for a 1st birthday party?
One-year-olds don't sit through a show, so the entertainment needs to be something they can move around in. Toddler play hire, a small soft play set and a ball pit work far better than a performer. Many families add a face painter or balloon twister for older cousins and siblings, and keep the whole event to about two hours around the baby's nap.
Do I need insurance or council approval for a jumping castle?
For a private party at home you generally don't need council approval, but the supplier should hold their own public liability insurance and be able to send you a certificate of currency. Ask about anchoring on grass versus hard surfaces, whether an operator stays on site, and what happens if it's windy or wet. For a park, school or public event, the venue will usually ask for that certificate plus a risk assessment before the booking is confirmed.
Can I book entertainment and party hire from one place?
Yes — that's the point of Kids Party House. Instead of contacting an entertainer, a castle company and a soft play business separately, you describe the party once: your suburb, date, your child's age and what you'd like. We match that to suppliers who cover your area and are free on the day, so you compare complete party options rather than piecing them together yourself.
Which areas do you cover?
We currently cover New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia, with dedicated area pages for the major metropolitan and regional markets — including Sydney, Parramatta, Liverpool, Campbelltown, Blacktown, Penrith, Newcastle and Wollongong in NSW, plus Melbourne, Brisbane, the Gold Coast and Perth. If your suburb isn't listed yet, send your brief and we'll tell you which suppliers travel to you.
